questions.question: Why does the Module 1 classifier break DRY even though no line is copied?
options: Two methods both rely on the fact that probabilities follow CATEGORIES order.
questions.explanation: DRY is about knowledge. The order rule is needed in both methods, so changing it means changing both.

questions.question: Which pair is orthogonal in the Module 2 code?
options: The classifier and the website module
questions.explanation: You can change how websites are read without touching keyword counting, and the reverse. The other pairs share knowledge.

questions.question: When is splitting a function a good idea?
options: When it is longer than ten lines
When it has more than one if
Always, because short functions are simpler
When the parts use different knowledge and can be understood alone
questions.explanation: A split pays off when each part can be read and changed on its own. Length alone is not a reason.
